recent_posts.title: Symbolic regression > black-box ML? What EML says about simpler AI
recent_posts.summary: A post exploring symbolic regression as an alternative to black-box ML models, centered around a minimal operator called EML (exp(x) − ln(y)). The argument is that some problems are better solved by discovering the actual underlying formula rather than approximating outputs with neural networks. Key themes include interpretability, reduced infrastructure cost, and the value of simpler, structured AI approaches over complex deep learning stacks.

recent_posts.title: CMS Trends 2026: What Matters and What's Just Hype
recent_posts.summary: A practitioner-focused breakdown of CMS trends heading into 2026. Key signals: composability fatigue is growing with unclear ROI on integrations, WordPress faces flanking from Shopify and Webflow rather than direct death, and AI earns its place in CMS only for asset tagging and personalization — not content production. The most underrated trend is Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): Gartner projects a 25% drop in search query volume by 2026 as AI chatbots absorb intent, making clean semantic content models a distribution strategy, not just good architecture.

recent_posts.title: Astro + AI vs WordPress for simple content sites
recent_posts.summary: A comparison of Astro (with AI assistance) versus WordPress for running a simple, expert-focused content site. WordPress remains the default for teams needing a traditional CMS with admin UI, plugins, and multi-role workflows. Astro becomes viable when paired with intentional process: Markdown, content collections, git-based editing, and deploy previews. AI lowers the operational cost of skipping a full editorial stack by helping with drafting, SEO fields, and metadata before publish. The key distinction is workflow consolidation (WordPress) versus repo-based content with fewer runtime layers (Astro). Astro plus AI fits small editing teams with simple content models who prioritize performance and control; WordPress wins when teams expect a traditional admin without developer involvement in every change.

recent_posts.title: Ignorance is Bliss
recent_posts.summary: AI is fundamentally changing the pace of software development, and ignoring it is no longer a viable option. While AI tools accelerate output for juniors and seniors alike, they don't replace system thinking, architectural judgment, or ownership of consequences. The real risks lie in hidden costs: debugging AI-generated code, architectural inconsistencies, and overconfidence. AI excels at prototyping, drafting specs, and repetitive work, but cannot define system boundaries or long-term trade-offs. CMS platforms like WordPress are already integrating AI deeply, signaling that AI is becoming part of the system itself. Developers who understand both systems and AI will have a decisive advantage; those who ignore it risk falling behind rapidly rather than gradually.

recent_posts.title: Em Dash: a programmable CMS experiment, not a WordPress replacement (yet)
recent_posts.summary: Em Dash is an early-stage, developer-oriented CMS that takes an API-first, tool-driven approach to content management, integrating with AI agents via MCP-like interfaces and using Astro on the frontend. Unlike traditional CMS platforms, it treats content as something operated on programmatically rather than edited through a UI. It features an isolated worker-based security model (requiring paid Cloudflare Workers for full benefit) and includes a WordPress content importer. In practice, local MCP integration had issues but API-based usage with Claude worked. The verdict: no plugin ecosystem, no non-dev editor experience, and significant infra requirements make it a developer experiment rather than a WordPress replacement — but it hints at where programmable, AI-driven content systems may be heading.

recent_posts.title: DatoCMS Explains Its Deliberate Non-AI-First Headless CMS Approach
recent_posts.summary: DatoCMS explains why it has deliberately avoided an 'AI-first' approach despite industry trends. Rather than filling its dashboard with AI writing assistants and SEO tools, the company focuses on opt-in AI features that users genuinely choose to use. Key concerns include data residency and security, particularly for European enterprise clients whose content would be routed through LLMs without explicit consent. DatoCMS does use AI internally (Claude Code) and has shipped AI-friendly APIs, an MCP server, and an AI translations plugin, but keeps these out of the core experience. The post frames this as a principled stance: prioritizing genuinely useful, transparent AI integrations over feature additions driven by industry pressure.

recent_posts.title: Why Twenty CRM’s Choice of Svelte Matters Architecturally
recent_posts.summary: Twenty, an open-source CRM, chose Svelte over React for its frontend — a decision with real architectural implications. Svelte's compile-time reactivity eliminates the virtual DOM, reducing runtime overhead and bundle size, which matters for data-heavy CRM interfaces. The post argues that Svelte's simpler mental model and less boilerplate reduce long-term cognitive load in large, long-lived applications. The trade-off is a smaller ecosystem compared to React, but the choice reflects a prioritization of performance and simplicity over ecosystem momentum. The author also notes a broader trend toward compile-time-first frameworks like Svelte and SolidJS as frontend complexity plateaus.

recent_posts.title: Sanity TypeGen Reaches General Availability
recent_posts.summary: Sanity TypeGen has reached general availability with Sanity Studio v5, providing precise TypeScript type generation from content schemas and GROQ queries. Key features include automatic type regeneration, stable APIs, consolidated configuration in `sanity.cli.ts`, faster generation via memoization, smarter output with preserved casing and correct key quoting, and reduced output size using an `ArrayOf` utility type. New `Get` and `FilterByType` utilities support complex schemas, and framework support now extends to `.svelte` and `.vue` files alongside `.astro`. The GA milestone guarantees API stability with no expected breaking changes to configuration, CLI commands, or utility types.

recent_posts.title: Custom 2FA implementation in Payload CMS

The approach focuses on extending Payload's authentication system without extensive code overwrites.
